- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-0.33), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- Model consistently under-responds to sharp upward sentiment spikes; if sentiment jumps to 1.00 within 3 days, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast horizon.
- Model over-anticipates downward moves after strong bullish sentiment; if sentiment drops to 0.00 after 1.00, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 3 days.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 3-day moving average of forecast vs true is negative, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid under-correction.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true trend by 2–5 days; if sentiment is trending upward, shift forecast 1–2 days ahead with slight overshoot (max +1.5%).
- Overshoot after spikes (e.g., 68+ → 69+ → 70+) is common; cap forecast at +1.5% above peak unless sentiment remains bullish.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) for 3+ days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 5 days.
